result.title: Benchmarking LLM abilities on postdoc-level natural science problems
result.summary: Scientific problems have no answer key, so evaluating an agent means deciding what counts as a better solution before any agent is run. Existing benchmarks either match a symbolic answer against a key or, where they require executable work, score it by unit tests, by a rubric, or by position on a competition leaderboard. None of these is the criterion by which a field decides that one published method beats another. STEMBench adopts that criterion directly. Each of its twelve research problems in high-energy physics, astrophysics and neuroscience is scored by its own field's figure of merit, and each comes with two measured anchors: a submission that uses no domain knowledge, and an expert reference reproducing a published method, both obtained by running code shipped with the benchmark. The interval between them states how much of a problem is crossed by scientific insight rather than by engineering. Across eight frontier models, task-level wins and domain-level leadership dissociate: a model that wins five of the twelve tasks leads no domain mean. In the high-effort cross-model comparison, at least one model's mean score exceeds the expert anchor on seven of twelve tasks. The remaining five span uncertainty estimation, latent and causal inference, and cross-site clinical classification. Numerical scores and official-submission validity capture different aspects of performance and are reported separately. We release the tasks, graders, anchors and harness.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 STEMBench，用高能物理、天体物理与神经科学共十二个研究级问题，按各自领域的品质因数（figure of merit）评分，并为每题配「无领域知识」与「复现已发表方法」两个实测锚点来界定科学洞察所能跨越的区间。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无标准答案 + 双锚点 + 领域内在品质因数」的评分设计，可能为缺乏参考轨迹的 latent 推理过程打分提供可供核查的评价思路；论文本身不涉及视觉状态或多模态推理。
